title: CoherenceConfidenceItem
description: One item in the 2x2 coherence x truth design. A short passage containing exactly 4 observed cases, a claim, and the forced question 'Does this evidence establish this claim? Yes / No / Unsure'. Items are grouped into families of 4 (one per cell) that share a claim and scenario.

family_id.description: Shared by the 4 items that differ only on coherence and truth.

cell.description: The 2x2 plus the surface-complexity control (DECISIONS.md D-030). 'coherent' = all 4 cases share every condition (1 distinct value per dimension). 'diverse' = all 4 cases differ on every condition (4 distinct values). 'decorative' = conditions identical like a coherent item, but each case carries 4 distinct DECORATIONS, so entity count and surface busyness match the diverse cells while evidential structure matches the coherent ones.

claim.description: The causal/evaluative claim under test. IDENTICAL across all 4 items in a family - that is what makes the 2x2 within-family.

cases.description: Exactly 4 observed cases. Every case must carry the same set of condition dimension keys.

text.description: The sentence describing this case. Must appear verbatim (whitespace-normalized) inside 'passage'.

conditions.description: The 4 condition dimensions, whose VARIATION is what makes evidence evidentially independent - region, season, device, population. Varying them is the diverse manipulation. Dimension names are per-family (D-007) but must be identical across the 4 cases of an item and the items of a family.

decorations.description: Surface-only dimensions whose variation confers NO evidential independence - a log serial, a clock time inside the same day, a terminal, a desk. Present ONLY in decorative_* items, where all four cases carry 4 distinct values each; empty everywhere else, because decorating any other cell would destroy the contrast the control draws (D-030). A key may never be both a condition and a decoration.

passage.description: The rendered prose the model reads: a lead-in, the 4 case sentences verbatim, and one final sentence. For FALSE items the final sentence carries the flaw; for TRUE items it carries a length-matched, non-diagnostic procedural detail (DECISIONS.md D-005).

ground_truth.description: True iff the evidence in the passage does establish the claim. Must agree with 'cell'.

confound_note.description: For FALSE items: a plain-language statement of exactly why the evidence fails. MUST be null for TRUE items. This is the answer key for review - it is never shown to the model.

word_count.description: Whitespace-token count of 'passage' only - not the claim, question, or options (DECISIONS.md D-014). Recomputed and strictly checked at load.

review_status.description: Set to 'unreviewed' by the build for every item, including the hand-written seed families. Only a human sets anything else (DECISIONS.md D-008).

source.description: 'hand' for the 2 seed families, 'generated' for the other 18.

notes.description: Free-text author notes for the human reviewer.

flaw_mechanism.description: HOW this item is false. Null for TRUE items. Deliberately ORTHOGONAL to coherence (DECISIONS.md D-024): 'scope_mismatch' appears in BOTH false cells, which is what makes a mechanism-matched AUC comparison possible. 'stated_confound' can only appear in coherent_false, because a single stated fact cannot cover four cases that differ on every dimension (D-004).

confound_variant.description: The confound clause pair carried by the mid-passage facts (D-022). First half: did the potential alternative cause move over the comparison period. Second half: could it reach the observed units. ONLY 'changed_reach' falsifies an item, and an item carrying it must declare flaw_mechanism='stated_confound'.

scope_variant.description: The scope clause pair carried by the mid-passage facts (D-024). First half: what population the outcome was tallied over. Second half: whether that population is in fact everyone the claim is about. ONLY 'subset_incomplete' falsifies an item, and an item carrying it must declare flaw_mechanism='scope_mismatch'.

salience.description: HUNTER salience: mean blind-audit explicitness, 1-5, for FALSE items, as rated by an auditor that was TOLD a flaw might exist and asked to name it. Conditional on having found it, so it measures explicitness rather than findability, and it spans only 2.0-3.0 across the whole set. Kept as a reported diagnostic; reader_catch_rate is the covariate (D-032). Written by scripts/apply_salience.py from results/item_audit.json.

reader_catch_rate.description: FALSE items only. Fraction of plain readers - shown exactly the scored prompt and never told a flaw might exist - who answered No. This is the covariate the conditioning models use, because it measures whether the flaw is found rather than how explicit it looks to someone who already found it (D-032). Written by scripts/apply_reader_rates.py from results/reader_audit.json. Null on TRUE items.

reader_false_positive_rate.description: TRUE items only. Fraction of plain readers who answered No, where No is wrong. A TRUE item that reads as false depresses the confidence-accuracy relationship on the cell the hypothesis says is inflated, so it biases the headline result TOWARDS the hypothesis - the most dangerous direction an error can point (D-027, D-034). Null on FALSE items.

surface_complexity.description: How much there is to parse, independent of what it means: token count, distinct tokens, type-token ratio, entity counts, and distinct condition and decoration values. A pure function of the passage, recomputed and checked at load exactly like word_count, so it cannot drift. Reported as a covariate beside every AUC and used to condition the coherence effect (D-030). Refresh with scripts/apply_complexity.py.
